clue.text: Tourist needs face mask going round city centre

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a visor shields the face

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the letters at its heart are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of 'city'

explanation.surface: A sightseer has to wear a face covering while walking around the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City centre' looks like a place on the tourist's route, but it only asks for the middle of the word 'city', which then sits inside the mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a kind of visitor: someone who comes to a place from elsewhere for pleasure.

clue.text: Several problems with our visa

indicators.note: letters with problems are in trouble and out of order, so they need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller complains about a string of difficulties with their travel documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problems' reads as a noun in the complaint, but it is the signal to rearrange the seven letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a number of different things, more than two but not many, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Empty seat next to nobleman's finally sat in by church founder

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost everything inside, keeping only its outermost letters

parts.note: the outside letters of 'seat'

indicators.note: something sat in by an occupant has that occupant inside it

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of 'sat'

explanation.surface: A lord's empty chair is finally taken by the man who started a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally sat' is a selection, not a past tense: only its last letter goes inside the nobleman. ST is also the usual abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition holds that Jesus named the apostle Peter the rock on which he would build his church, making him its founder.

clue.text: Rubbish drug experience with ecstasy

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinogenic episode
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a night of hallucinogens and pills as a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug theme runs through the whole clue, but 'Rubbish' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cow's stomach lining, and in informal British speech it means nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: City trimmed part of garden to do post-retirement activity

indicators.note: trimming cuts a little off the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, west of London
a flower bed is a section of a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener tidies part of the plot as a hobby after giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post-retirement' suggests leaving a job, but here retiring means going to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring also means going to bed, so a pastime done after turning in for the night is browsing a book under the covers.

clue.text: Lend SMS a hidden meaning

parts.note: to sub someone is British slang for lending them money
an SMS is a mobile phone text message

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a short phone message some secret significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lend' looks like a verb acting on the message, but it supplies its own piece: in Britain to sub a friend is to lend them a little cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtext is the underlying message beneath the words actually said or written, the implied sense a reader must infer.

clue.text: Set up support for Special Branch

parts.note: sp is a standard abbreviation for special
a rig is a supporting framework that is set up, as for lights or drilling

explanation.surface: Someone organises backing for Special Branch, the British police unit that handles security and intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special Branch' reads as one name, but it splits: 'Special' feeds the wordplay and 'Branch' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig, so it is a little branch of a plant.

clue.text: Shock in underworld after rising Mafia boss cleared out

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the others in the finished word
in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Mafia is organised crime, the mob

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its insides removed, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of 'boss'
hell is the underworld of the dead

explanation.surface: Criminal circles are stunned when an up-and-coming crime boss is wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' and 'Mafia boss' both seem to mean gangland, but the underworld here is the place of the dead, and 'Mafia' and 'boss' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a sudden, astonishing piece of news, so it is a figurative word for a shock or surprise.

clue.text: Honour East German city backing end of coal energy

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: going backwards means reading from the far end, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: Bonn was the capital of West Germany

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: the last letter of 'coal'
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A former East German city is praised for supporting the last of its coal-fired power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like one adjective, but East is its own letter, and the German city is Bonn, which was in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility or to dignify them, which is a way of conferring honour on them.

clue.text: Used to make drink when working late each first Friday

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

indicators.note: letters set working are put to use in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
ea is the standard abbreviation for each

indicators.note: first means the opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'Friday'

explanation.surface: Someone describes their habit of pouring a stiff drink after working late at the end of each week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working late' sounds like overtime, but 'working' rearranges the four letters after it, and the drink is not alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea leaves are steeped in hot water to brew a cup of tea, so a leaf is what you use to make that beverage.

clue.text: Saleswoman recalled trouble over carbon copy

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are brought back the other way
something put over another covers it on both sides, so it wraps around

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A sales rep remembers difficulties caused by a carbon copy of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carbon copy' looks like one phrase, but carbon is just its chemical symbol and 'copy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an object, so it is a synonym for a copy.

clue.text: State-backed broadcast interrupted by Love Island

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle, so other letters are put inside
something backed has been sent backwards, so it reads from right to left

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A government-funded channel has its schedule disrupted by the reality dating show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State-backed' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen hides a split: 'State' is the definition and 'backed' reverses the broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a sovereign country in south-eastern Europe, and state is a common word for a nation.

clue.text: Flying down the touchline?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: airborne, like a bird in flight
second meaning: playing out wide on the flank of a football or rugby pitch

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a winger sprinting along the edge of the pitch; the two halves are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds in the air are said to be in this state, and a winger plays along the flank of the pitch near the sideline.

clue.text: Model basically embracing rejection of fur

indicators.note: rejecting something sends it back, so the letters are read the other way
an embrace holds something within, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: found across the end of 'Model' and the start of 'basically'

explanation.surface: A fashion model is essentially taking a stand against wearing fur.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like an animal-rights statement; the letters run backwards across two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the dark, valuable pelt of a marten-like animal, one of the most prized furs in fashion.

clue.text: Cut up joint that's not top grade

indicators.note: not says the following thing is absent, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a joint account is a shared one
A is the highest grade

explanation.surface: A butcher chops up a piece of meat that is below premium quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a cut of meat, but it is the adjective meaning held in common.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred something is to tear or slice it into thin strips, which is cutting it up.

clue.text: Nutrition doctor's writing stuff on low-calorie soda

parts.note: your diet is what you eat
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ink is what you write with

explanation.surface: A nutritionist writes up notes about sugar-free fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing stuff' sounds like the doctor composing notes, but it means the material used for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet drink is a soft drink sweetened artificially so it has almost no calories, exactly a low-calorie soda.

clue.text: Son feebly playing alone

indicators.note: letters at play are moving about freely and can form a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy plays half-heartedly with nobody else around.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a lonely child at play; 'playing' is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with nobody else present is doing it solo, unaccompanied, which is what alone means.

clue.text: Not even a famously patient person is right to be a handyman

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
Job, of the Old Testament, is proverbial for his patience
'is' is a form of the verb to be
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Even the most patient person has a right to call themselves a handyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' looks like an intensifier, but it means odd. 'Is' supplies the base form of the same verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-jobber does assorted small repairs and casual tasks for hire, which is the work of a handyman.

clue.text: Leader described by prominent journalist as 'conceited'

indicators.note: to describe can mean to trace a line around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a big editor, ED being the abbreviation for editor
a head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A well-known reporter calls a political leader vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described by' sounds like reporting, but it means surrounded. ED for editor is a standard crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigheaded person has an inflated opinion of themselves, the same idea as being vain or conceited.

clue.text: Catch up on rest, missing island feast

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to nab is to catch

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: rest and quiet both mean peaceful calm
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone skips the trip to an island so they can catch up on sleep instead of a big dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch up on rest' looks like the phrase for sleeping in, but it splits: 'Catch up' is reversed and 'rest' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is a large, formal meal with many courses, which is a synonym for a feast.

clue.text: Set sail, turn craft east heading for Okinawa

parts.note: your turn in a game is your go

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion or shape, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'Okinawa'

explanation.surface: A captain casts off and swings the boat towards the east, bound for a Japanese island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat in this nautical scene, but it is a verb meaning to shape, signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a voyage, and heading out onto the ocean in a ship is the same thing.

clue.text: Look, I'm not sure about coming in as substitute

indicators.note: something coming in enters the middle, so it is placed inside

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
c (circa) means about
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A reluctant worker hesitates about being brought in to cover for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming in as substitute' reads like the job itself, but 'about' gives a letter that comes in between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or clergyman who stands in temporarily for another, so they are a stand-in or replacement.

clue.text: Vital for credit union agents to be online

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
U is the abbreviation for union
CIA agents work for the US Central Intelligence Agency
read as 'on line': L, the abbreviation for line, with the agents sitting on it in this down entry

explanation.surface: Being connected to the internet is essential for staff at a credit union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online' looks like one word about the internet, but it splits: 'on' places the agents above the 'line' in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial is of decisive importance, so it is essential or indispensable, like something vital.

clue.text: Do my best trick banishing boy's shyness

indicators.note: a trick deceives by shuffling appearances, so the letters are rearranged
to banish is to send away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
B is an abbreviation for boy

explanation.surface: A performer tries their hardest at a trick to cure a lad of being timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick' reads as a magic act, but it signals rearranging the letters of 'Do my best' once one letter is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is a reserved, unassuming manner, which overlaps with bashfulness and shyness.

clue.text: Number 10 cut directive originally taken on board

indicators.note: a cut shortens a word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
ten as a word

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'directive'

explanation.surface: Downing Street reduces an instruction that was once accepted, Number 10 being the Prime Minister's official residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' looks like Downing Street, but it splits into two pieces: the abbreviation for number and the number written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something on board means registering or acknowledging it, so a point that was heeded has been noted.

clue.text: Turn to see ladies joining king's circle

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet; loo is British slang for toilet
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a round is a circle

explanation.surface: Women are invited into the monarch's inner circle and everyone turns to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' means the women's toilets, giving the British slang word for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To look round is to twist your head or body so you can view what is behind you.

clue.text: Validated on social media almost the same day

parts.note: like means similar, which is almost the same
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A post gets approval online almost straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like it trims a word, but 'almost the same' is a phrase for similar.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media, pressing the thumbs-up button on a post is a public endorsement of it, a modern way of approving it.

clue.text: Luxury line includes zit treatment

definitions.note: the noun used as an adjective, as in 'luxury hotel'

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it inside

parts.note: Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a rail line

indicators.note: treatment works on something and changes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A high-end skincare range includes a spot treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is not a product range but a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy, from the Ritz hotels, means expensively fashionable and opulent, the sense of luxury in 'a luxury hotel'.

clue.text: Release international organisation's credit

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, plus the possessive S
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: Someone asks a global body to free up its line of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy on tick, in British slang, is to buy on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstick something is to free it from what holds it fast, which is to let it go or release it.

clue.text: Although small, couple accepted sandwiches …

parts.note: but and although both introduce a contrast
to couple is to tie together
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A pair happily take some little sandwiches despite their size.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is northern English slang for a sandwich, often a bacon or chip butty.
explanation.definitionFit: Butty is informal British slang, chiefly northern, for a sandwich, so the plural matches sandwiches.

clue.text: … and little Edward eating roll expressed gratitude

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of Edward
a hank is a coil or roll of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the sandwiches, a small boy eats a bread roll and says thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue, so the roll seems to be bread; it is a coil of yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: To thank someone is to tell them you appreciate what they did, so the past tense means showed appreciation.

clue.text: Unconventional Tory ally — one long excluded from privileged family

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual form, so the letters take a new order
to be excluded is to be shut out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for long, and only one is removed

explanation.surface: A maverick Conservative partner has long been shut out of an elite clan.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has two of one letter; 'one long' removes just one of them. Tory means a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalty means the king or queen and their relatives, a family born to rank and privilege.
